paragraphs.heading: A rebirth of old ideas
paragraphs.text: The word Renaissance means "rebirth". It names a period and a cultural movement in Europe that came at the close of the Late Middle Ages and the start of the early modern era. Some date it to the 15th and 16th centuries, while others stretch it from the 14th century to the 17th. Its mark was a revival of the writing, thinking and art of classical antiquity, which Europeans rediscovered.

paragraphs.heading: Humanism at its core
paragraphs.text: The movement rested on humanism, an outlook built from the Roman idea of humanitas and from rediscovered Greek philosophy. Humanist scholars such as Poggio Bracciolini hunted through monastery libraries for ancient Latin texts. After Constantinople fell in 1453, Greek scholars fled west carrying precious manuscripts, many of them long forgotten in Western Europe. Humanists did not turn away from Christianity, and the Church paid for a great deal of Renaissance art.

paragraphs.heading: Starting in Florence
paragraphs.text: The Renaissance first took hold in Florence, one of many Italian states, and then spread across Italy and later Europe. Many trace its ideas to Florence around 1300, in the writing of Dante and Petrarch and the painting of Giotto. Explanations for why it began there point to the city's politics, the patronage of its leading family, the Medici, and the arrival of Greek scholars. Venice, Genoa, Milan, Rome and Naples became other major centers.

paragraphs.heading: New ways of seeing and writing
paragraphs.text: In art, Florentine painters led by Masaccio tried to show the human body realistically and found ways to render depth and light more naturally. Linear perspective was one of several techniques for painting a more natural-looking reality. Authors also turned more and more to vernacular languages, alongside Latin and Greek. Together with the printing press, this put books, above all the Bible, in the hands of far more people.

paragraphs.heading: Beyond the arts
paragraphs.text: The changes reached well past painting. Machiavelli and other political thinkers set out to describe politics as it actually worked. The era helped shape the customs of diplomacy, and it saw revolutions in printing and navigation along with the arrival of modern banking and accounting. Thinkers like Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo, skilled in many fields, gave us the phrase "Renaissance man".

paragraphs.heading: A spark in 1401
paragraphs.text: Some writers give the Renaissance a precise birthday. In 1401 two rival artists, Lorenzo Ghiberti and Filippo Brunelleschi, competed to make the bronze doors of the Baptistery of Florence Cathedral, and Ghiberti won. Others see a broader contest among Brunelleschi, Ghiberti, Donatello and Masaccio for commissions as what sparked the creativity.

paragraphs.heading: Was it really a break
paragraphs.text: Historians still argue about what the Renaissance was. The older view treats it as a clean break from the past. Many historians now stress how much it carried on from the Middle Ages, and some question whether the label is useful at all. Panofsky described the two eras as linked "by a thousand ties".
